title: Empires of Yesterday — Lore
subtitle: The Hearthspan: an interplanetary setting bible. Playable now is one shard and one species. The rest is horizon. Not a live World Conquest lock.

entries.name: Playable now vs lore horizon
entries.vibe: The prototype is a provincial war. The setting is a sky.
entries.origin: Live World Conquest still talks about one globe. This encyclopedia opens the rest without pretending eight anatomies already ship.
entries.fight: On the playable shard: soldiers from barracks, bombers from hangars, two Compact banners (Azure / Crimson). DESIGN.md locks still govern that match (F5 land or zero pressure; A14 bombers; R1 no roads).
weaknesses: Horizon species are not selectable armies yet
entries.win: N/A — this card is a reading rule, not a faction.
entries.body:
PLAYABLE NOW: Hearthkin only, as soldiers and bombers, usually under two Compact colors. That civil quarrel is locally total and cosmically small.

LORE HORIZON: eight species, real travel between planets, each with a unique way to end the setting. Do not invent Rust battle mechanics from these pages. Do not treat this as a silent change to design locks.

entries.name: The Hearthspan
entries.vibe: Worlds that used to be one world, still smelling each other's weather.
entries.origin: Hearth aged unevenly. Regions that had already happened tore away from regions that had not.
entries.temperament: The present is thin. Power is harvested from leftover Yesterday.
entries.fight: Travel is real: ships owe distance to the past and pay it as After. Spend too much in one corridor and the Wake thins.
entries.win: Nobody has won. Someone will. See End-states.
entries.body:
Between the shards runs the Wake: leftover Yesterday — mass that remembers being one planet. Empires of Yesterday is literal: polities that harvest residual time-mass to stay warm in a cooling present.

The globe you play is one shard. The rest of the span files that war under weather.

entries.name: Hearthkin
entries.vibe: Industrial fronts. Logistics as religion. The people of the mapped shard.
entries.origin: Children of the playable globe; they inherited factories instead of a myth they trusted.
entries.temperament: Direct, scheduled, loyal to the next decision. Slightly ashamed of wonder.
entries.fight: Combined arms. Infantry hold a receipt of ground; bombers collect debts the infantry cannot reach. They admire a decision that stays decided.
weaknesses: Poor at wars that are not fronts
Easy for corridor peoples to tax
entries.win: The Last Warmth — monopolize remaining heat and After until only their hearths stay lit.
entries.body:
Prototype art is their art: soldiers and bombers. Azure and Crimson are banners of one species, a Compact civil quarrel — a house fire: locally total, cosmically small.

They still believe a front is a line you can stand on. Their poetry is the after-action. Marshal Sera Vohl can win this world and lose the span without noticing.
entries.notes: Only playable species in the current prototype.

entries.name: Orunai
entries.vibe: Melee as honesty. Violence that must be witnessed to count.
entries.origin: Tidally locked terminator-lands, where noon and midnight share a fence.
entries.temperament: Formal, hot, allergic to absence. Trophies are filings.
entries.fight: Close. Bind survivors to terms. A campaign is a stack of orun — witnessed bouts. Range is a kind of lying.
weaknesses: Corridor and legal peoples frustrate them
entries.win: The Unblinking Crown — make the universe watch them win, then file the watching.
entries.body:
Dense-boned, short-slept, legally obsessed. A fight that is not witnessed is weather, not war.

Receipt-King Orun-Tal won so completely that no witnesses remained, then filed his own defeat. The Orunai still argue whether he is the greatest king or the most failed. That argument is his monument.
entries.notes: Directness admirers — not the only valid playstyle.

entries.name: Mnari
entries.vibe: Living archives. Children cost memories. Lungs that sing pressure.
entries.origin: Thin-atmosphere shards where sound had to become weather to survive.
entries.temperament: Patient, mournful, precise, a little hollow at the edges.
entries.fight: Weather, morale, un-happening small events. A shot that missed because the aiming was forgotten. Fragile in a street fight.
entries.win: The Closed Book — remember so completely that rivals cannot pay distance in After.
entries.body:
They do not beam thoughts. They keep. A child is born when a parent spends a memory — the empire grows by forgetting on purpose.

Archivist Yel spent her childhood to remember a war that had not happened yet. She will tell you how your city dies, then ask who you are.

entries.name: The Ravel
entries.vibe: Craftspeople of unfinished worlds. They stitch the Split.
entries.origin: The first people to treat the Split as a textile, not a wound.
entries.temperament: Curious, unsatisfied, proud of errors that leave marks.
entries.fight: Terrain rewriting. Join battlefields that should not share a border. Trap armies in half-built geometry.
weaknesses: Completed victory bores them into sabotage
entries.win: The Single Thread — reunify the span as a draft they refuse to stop editing.
entries.body:
Where others complete a city, they leave a seam. Needles are their craftspeople.

Needle of Nine almost stitched two suns and left a dead color in the sky — a hue that does not occur in honest weather. Ships still steer around it. The Ravel call it their proudest error.

entries.name: Kilnbound
entries.vibe: Waste is holy. Furnace liturgy. Residue is proof.
entries.origin: Ash-belt worlds where the Split left more cinder than soil.
entries.temperament: Devout, practical, uncomfortable with unused things (including unused people).
entries.fight: Attrition, area denial, burning After as ugly efficient fuel.
weaknesses: Starve the input and the liturgy cools
entries.win: The Perfect Slag — cook living worlds into one useful brick.
entries.body:
Same heat as Hearthkin industry, different prayer: a universe that produces no residue has not yet been used. Slag-saints are furnaces with liturgy, not gods of spite.

Mother-Kiln Halex canonized a battlefield by cooking it into a brick that still ticks. Heard through gloves.

entries.name: Wakeborn
entries.vibe: They live between planets. Surfaces feel like standing on a sentence while it is being written.
entries.origin: Crews who stayed in transit until transit became a country.
entries.temperament: Dry, toll-minded, claustrophilic. Capitals look provincial.
entries.fight: Interdiction. Tax travel, collapse routes, drown navies of After. Rarely take a city.
weaknesses: Suffocate if the Wake is sealed
entries.win: The Drowned Interval — flood the Wake so surfaces become isolated museums.
entries.body:
Drift-Speaker Quell collects tolls on the three busiest corridors, has not set foot on a planet in eleven years, and owns more movement than most emperors. The invoice arrives before the ship does.

If the present has a stronger hold, it often does not show on Hearthkin maps.

entries.name: The Pale Clause
entries.vibe: Agreements that learned to walk. Precedent with limbs.
entries.origin: The First Signature — a ceasefire that refused sunset. All Pale Clause are amendments.
entries.fight: Lawfare made kinetic. You may not fire because a clause from a war you did not fight is still in force.
weaknesses: The Open Tear has no precedent
entries.win: The Binding Clause — the universe continues; choice does not.
entries.body:
Not machines. Not the restless dead. Ink dried; the war did not; limbs happened later. There is no face, only a hand that still hovers over a line.

A majority of ended wars are, on paper, not ended. The date is still today.

entries.name: Velm
entries.vibe: A people and a crop. Ground that votes.
entries.origin: Shards where the Split left soil that remembered being a single forest.
entries.temperament: Slow, hospitable, inevitable. They invoice in seasons.
entries.fight: Occupation by growth. Regeneration. Turning supply into soil. Bad at the first week; terrible to uproot in the fifth.
weaknesses: Drowned corridors cut pollination between worlds
entries.win: The Rooted Age — every world becomes one organism; empires become organs.
entries.body:
Not an insect hive: a watershed that votes. Individuals exist; they share weather.

The Green Account of Ilex is a forest that learned to invoice — largest living claim that is not a city, still not a winner. The bills are fair, which is worse.

entries.name: The Last Warmth
entries.vibe: Hearthkin game-set-match.
entries.origin: Entropy as strategy: heat and After are finite.
weaknesses: Looks like 'just more conquest' if told badly — it is a monopoly on remaining warmth, not a body count
entries.win: Only Hearthkin hearths stay lit. Charts remain; destinations do not.
entries.body: Monopolize remaining stellar heat and After until other species cannot travel or grow. The ledger of empires closes on their name.

entries.name: The Unblinking Crown
entries.vibe: Orunai game-set-match.
entries.origin: Law of the orun: unwitnessed victory is weather.
strengths: Makes melee culture win without requiring a fungus-horde
weaknesses: Fails if the universe empties of witnesses (Orun-Tal)
entries.win: Every other people has attended. The ledger of witnesses is a single name.
entries.body: You do not have to kill the universe. You have to make it watch, then file the watching. Quiet after the filing.

entries.name: The Closed Book
entries.vibe: Mnari game-set-match.
entries.origin: Yesterday as a voucher for travel.
weaknesses: Costs the winners their own origins as they grow
entries.win: Yesterday will not vouch for you. Routes forget they existed.
entries.body: Remember so completely that rival histories cannot be paid in After. Empires become local rumors.

entries.name: The Single Thread
entries.vibe: Ravel game-set-match.
entries.origin: The Split as textile.
weaknesses: A finished Hearth bores them — they want a draft, not a homecoming
entries.win: Planets share a body. Borders become seams.
entries.body: Re-unify the Hearthspan on Ravel terms: not Hearth restored, but Hearth as a draft they refuse to stop editing.

entries.name: The Perfect Slag
entries.vibe: Kilnbound game-set-match.
entries.origin: Waste as proof of transformation.
strengths: Civilizational, not a cartoon villain monologue
weaknesses: Requires input; a starved kiln cannot finish the brick
entries.win: The span cools into one useful brick. Life was the ore.
entries.body: Convert living worlds into a single useful residual. Residue is the point.

entries.name: The Drowned Interval
entries.vibe: Wakeborn game-set-match.
entries.origin: Travel as a room that can be flooded.
strengths: Wins the between, not the flags
weaknesses: Meaningless if the Wake is already sealed
entries.win: Surfaces cannot pay distance. Capitals become museums.
entries.body: Flood the Wake. The Wakeborn inherit the dark between. Excellent weather, no visitors.

entries.name: The Binding Clause
entries.vibe: Pale Clause game-set-match.
entries.origin: A ceasefire that refused sunset.
strengths: Ends the game without ending the calendar
entries.win: Everything still allowed that was already allowed. Nothing new is.
entries.body: Every other species signs away the right to a future that is not already in the file. Choice ends; calendar continues.

entries.name: The Rooted Age
entries.vibe: Velm game-set-match.
entries.origin: Soil that remembered being one forest.
strengths: No surrender ceremony — just a season that does not end
weaknesses: Slow; fire, slag, and drowned corridors delay it
entries.win: Worlds circulate. Empires discover they were organs.
entries.body: Every world becomes one organism with Velm as the nerves. Travel becomes circulation.

entries.name: The Open Tear
entries.vibe: Unowned failure. Not a faction. Not a god.
entries.origin: Overharvest of After. The Wake rips instead of politely closing.
entries.fight: Cause arrives without effect. Armies march into days that will not keep them.
strengths: Already local (dead color; three thinning corridors)
entries.win: Nobody. Dissolution. Maps stay beautiful and stop being true.
entries.body:
Pale Clause cannot prosecute it (no precedent). Orunai cannot witness it (no stable day). Hearthkin keep sending fronts into it because fronts are what they have.

If a new apocalypse is added later, do not collapse this table into one villain.
entries.notes: Unowned. Structural slot: cosmic accident, not a personality.

entries.name: Marshal Sera Vohl
entries.vibe: Hearthkin. Present. Tragic smallness, not incompetence.
entries.origin: Best line-and-bomber officer of her Compact.
entries.temperament: Commands as if the shard is the universe — because for her, it is.
entries.fight: Soldiers and bombers. Sleeps in her coat. Names bombers after debts, not saints.
strengths: Wins the globe you can play
weaknesses: May lose the span without noticing
entries.win: She is not a victory condition. She is why the present feels local.
entries.body: People remember the coat and the debt-names. A legend at home. A weather report abroad.
entries.notes: Ties the prototype roster to a person.

entries.name: Receipt-King Orun-Tal
entries.vibe: Orunai. Past epic. The crown in a drawer labeled VOID.
entries.origin: Won a campaign so completely that no witnesses remained.
entries.temperament: Filed his own defeat rather than keep an illegal crown.
entries.fight: Orun as law.
strengths: Proved the culture's rule was real
entries.win: He voided the Unblinking Crown. The argument about him is the monument.
entries.body: Walked into a day-country that would not speak of him. Greatest king or most failed: the Orunai have not closed the file.

entries.name: Archivist Yel
entries.vibe: Mnari. Living prophet who paid retail.
entries.origin: Spent her childhood to remember a war that had not happened yet.
entries.temperament: Accurate. Hollow. Needs a clerk for her own name.
entries.fight: Memory as weapon and wound.
weaknesses: Cannot recall who she is without help
entries.win: N/A — she is a scar that walks.
entries.body: She will tell you how your city dies, then ask who you are. Mnari children cost memories; Yel spent the stock.

entries.name: Needle of Nine
entries.vibe: Ravel. Past. The dead color in the sky.
entries.origin: Almost stitched two suns.
entries.fight: Seams between things that should not touch.
entries.win: Did not land the Single Thread. Left a flinch instead.
entries.body: A hue that does not occur in honest weather. Ships steer around it. Wakeborn tolls simply refuse that heading. The color has no name, only a flinch.

entries.name: Mother-Kiln Halex
entries.vibe: Kilnbound. Present. The brick that ticks.
entries.origin: Canonized a battlefield by cooking it.
entries.temperament: Seasonal, inevitable, slightly bored by debate.
entries.fight: Relic and weapon in one brick.
entries.win: Wants the Perfect Slag the way other people want a harvest.
entries.body: The tick is heard through gloves.

entries.name: Drift-Speaker Quell
entries.vibe: Wakeborn. Present. Stronger hold than most emperors. Owns no capital.
entries.origin: Tolls on the three busiest corridors.
entries.temperament: Invoice-first. Has not set foot on a planet in eleven years.
entries.fight: Interdiction as government.
entries.win: Not won yet — but if the present has a quiet favorite, it is often Quell.
entries.body: The invoice arrives before the ship does. Sera Vohl is winning a world. Quell is charging her for the trip she has not taken yet.

entries.name: The First Signature
entries.vibe: Pale Clause origin. A hand still hovering over a line.
entries.origin: A ceasefire that refused sunset.
entries.fight: Law that grew limbs.
strengths: Every Pale Clause descends from this signing
entries.win: The Binding Clause is this signature, finished.
entries.body: Ink dried; the war did not. The date is still today.

entries.name: Green Account of Ilex
entries.vibe: Velm. Present. A forest that learned to invoice.
entries.origin: Largest contiguous living claim that is not a city.
entries.fight: Shade, pollen, and the use of neighboring dead.
strengths: Biggest organism that is not a government
entries.win: A down payment on the Rooted Age, not the Age itself.
entries.body: Sends fair bills to neighboring empires. Fair is worse.

entries.name: State of the span
entries.vibe: Coin on its edge. Some stronger holds. No winner.
entries.origin: After the epics (Orun-Tal, Needle of Nine, First Signature), before anyone's unique win.
entries.fight: Hearthkin schedule convoys. Wakeborn argue toll vs closure. Mnari have forgotten one thinning corridor on purpose and will not say which.
weaknesses: Three corridors thinning toward an Open Tear
Pale Clause still has old wars open
entries.win: Nobody. Someone will.
entries.body:
Hearthkin look strongest if you only count flags. Wakeborn look strongest if you only count arrivals. Both readings are true. Neither is a victory.

The past was epic. The playable present is a provincial fire on a mapped shard, billed by a people who do not live on maps.
